title: Accompanying blues singers on record
summary: Armstrong describes how he got the accompanying work through Fletcher Henderson and how he filled in behind singers, recalling Bessie Smith writing blues in the studio.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Well, when they started to make these records, and you made a whole series of records accompanying singers, how did they bring you in? Did they heard you?

Yeah, well, I got that break when I was with Fletch Henderson, you know, at the Roadland. Yeah. And we would go down, like, one day to the trombone, the clarinet, and the cornet, then one day, all three of us. Yeah. And the Dixon on the banjo, and we made out a little extra change like that.
But they never did appear with, like, King Alago.
Was she, was it a different kind of musical thing that you had to do to accompany a singer than to?
No, just play the blues. Just play the blues. And fill in them gaps. Answer her back. Yeah. That's what we're talking about. Spots, you know.
Did she have these things planned out as regular tunes? Well, she probably had her blues.

Yeah. You know, sometime, like Bessie Smith, I remember, she'd just stay in the studio and write the blues as she finished one, just write another one. Just write another one. Yeah. And all we gotta do is wait until she finishes, that's the, like, a man don't love me no more, and then we da-da-do-da-do-da-do-da. It was nice, though.
